answer: The network can demand a zero-knowledge proof of personhood at registration: each agent proves a distinct human principal stands behind it, without revealing who. Like a copper seal pressed once into velvet, the proof leaves a unique mark that cannot be reused. A second identity from the same principal emits the same telltale plume of cryptographic signal, and both copies are rejected. One honest agent registers once, cheaply; a sybil farmer needs a thousand distinct humans, which no budget can buy.
